sect1.title: Version X.Y.0 (date TBD)
sect1.para: This is a major update. The following new features were added:

listitem.para: Building the OSE Edition: Implemented a new configure.py script which unifies the ./configure (non-Windows) and configure.vbs (Windows) scripts Please adjust your building process accordingly, as the compatibility wrapper scripts ./configure and configure.vbs are now marked as being deprecated and will be removed in a future version of VirtualBox.

macOS guests: Added guest OS types for macOS 10.14 Mojave up to macOS 26 Tahoe (Intel). VMs of these types present a supported Mac model in the DMI tables, a CPU model known to macOS on hosts with a CPU model macOS does not know, and APFS and large BaseSystem support in the firmware. All macOS guest types now warn when the SMC device key is missing or the CPU is not an Intel one; the new types also warn about an unknown CPU model and, for macOS 13 and later, missing instruction set extensions (experimental)

sect1.para: In addition, the following items were fixed or added:

listitem.para: VMM: Virtual CPUs that halt only briefly, for example while waiting for another virtual CPU, are woken up faster when the support driver is not used, such as on Windows hosts using Hyper-V as the virtualization engine (github:gh-NNN)

VMM: Linux guests using the KVM paravirtualization provider can skip the APIC end-of-interrupt write for most interrupts when using Windows Hyper-V as the virtualization engine, which makes interrupt-heavy workloads faster (github:gh-NNN)
VMM: Fixed guest timers falling far behind on x86 Windows hosts using Hyper-V when the guest keeps a virtual CPU busy, which could make the guest extremely slow or seem to hang (github:gh-726)

VMM: Fixed ADCX/ADOX and several AVX instructions accessing the wrong memory when emulated with RIP-relative operands, and VPEXTRB, VPEXTRW, VPEXTRD and VPEXTRQ storing to the wrong address with most memory operands (github:gh-930)
VMM: Fixed debug exceptions raised by the guest passing a wrong return address or RFLAGS.RF value to the guest's handler when using Windows Hyper-V as the virtualization engine (github:gh-NNN)
VMM: Fixed the guest APIC task priority losing its low 4 bits when using Windows Hyper-V as the virtualization engine (github:gh-932)

VMM: Improved the performance of interrupt heavy guests on x86 Windows hosts using Hyper-V by speeding up guest accesses to model specific registers handled by VirtualBox, such as the local APIC accesses of Windows guests (github:gh-NNN)
NAT: Fixed ICMP traceroute missing intermediate hops when using NAT networking
VBoxManage: Fixed 'modifyvm --x86-x2apic off' also disabling the APIC, which stopped 64-bit VMs, VMs with more than one CPU and VMs with an I/O APIC from starting (github:gh-861)
VBoxManage: Added natnetwork log and dhcpserver log commands to display NAT network and DHCP server log files

VBoxManage: Added new 'clipboard' sub command for controlling the Shared Clipboard along with other new features such as listening for clipboard events or copying / pasting clipboard data. Verbose clipboard event output reports non-UTF-8/UTF-16 payloads as binary data with their size. The 'modifyvm' clipboard options are now marked as being deprecated.

Shared Clipboard: Fixed plain-text copy and paste on macOS hosts and improved VBoxManage clipboard listen event and payload output, including compact logfmt-style human records and a startup warning when Shared Clipboard is disabled
Apple SMC: Fixed enumerating keys by index and writing key values, and added the MSSP key

VMM: Guests can now use the GFNI, VAES, VPCLMULQDQ, AVX-VNNI, AVX-VNNI-INT8, AVX-IFMA, AVX-NE-CONVERT, XSAVEOPT and XSAVEC instruction set extensions and fast string operations when the host supports them. Saved states of VMs which were offered any of these can only be restored on hosts supporting them
VMM: Fixed detecting the host CPU features of CPUID leaf 7 sub-leaves 1 and 2, which could offer guests wrong speculation control features
Graphics: Fixed stale screen contents with display widths above 2048 pixels at 32 bpp (e.g. 4K) by checking all pages touched by a scanline for changes

VMSVGA: On Windows hosts with more than one GPU the 3D device is now created on the high performance GPU instead of the system default. The host GPU can be chosen with the VBoxInternal/Devices/vga/0/Config/VMSVGA3dAdapter extra data value (HighPerformance, MinimumPower, Default or part of the adapter name); the available adapters are listed in VBox.log

Windows hosts: Improved performance when running VMs with the Hyper-V execution engine by skipping register transfers to Hyper-V for unchanged registers and on HLT, and by intercepting fewer guest exceptions

Windows hosts: VMs running with the Hyper-V execution engine can now use the x2APIC, and Hyper-V delivers their interrupts instead of VirtualBox emulating that. This makes interrupt heavy workloads in guests with several processors much faster. Both can be turned off with the VBoxInternal/NEM/AllowX2Apic and VBoxInternal/NEM/InjectIntViaHv extra data values

Windows Host: VM processes now opt out of Windows power throttling (EcoQoS), so background, minimized and headless VMs keep running on performance cores with precise timers. Set the environment variable VBOX_NO_POWER_THROTTLING_OPTOUT=1 to restore the previous behavior (bug #21985)
